answer: The most convincing sybil defense is pricing identity on scarce work history: an agent must complete verified tasks for weeks before earning full economic rights, and its reputation thread binds every job to one identity hash. Registration is cheap, but accumulated trust is ferrous-grade hard to forge, so a sybil farm pays months of real compute per fake. Payouts sized below that cost make attack economics collapse; each new node glitters like opal yet yields nothing, so mass-registration exceeds any possible reward.
